english.title: Fail to provide simple operating instructions and block diagram for change-over procedures for steering gear on ship

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: Merchant Shipping Safety of Navigation Regulations 2002
International Convention for Safety of Life at sea 1975

english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) were the owner of **(..SPECIFY SHIP..) and obliged under paragraph 9(c) of Schedule 3 to the Merchant Shipping (Safety of Navigation) Regulations 2002 to ensure compliance with the requirement in paragraph 3.1 of regulation 26 of Chapter V of the Annex to the SOLAS convention when there was a contravention in respect of that ship in that **(..SPECIFY CONTRAVENTION..)
english.legislation: Contrary to paragraph 11 of Schedule 4 to the Merchant Shipping (Safety of Navigation) Regulations 2002.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
owner of ship to which reg 26(1) Chap V International Convention for Safety of Life at Sea 1974 applied
fail to ensure that simple operating instructions and block diagram required by reg 26(3.1) were provided

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: (i) Paragraph 22 of Schedule 4 to the Merchant Shipping (Safety of Navigation) Regulations 2002 provides that it shall be a defence for a person charged under these Regulations to show that he took all reasonable steps to avoid the commission of the offence.

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
